facts.claim: A traveller can rest safely at Riverwalk.
Riverwalk can be seen from far off.
Riverwalk sells goods and services to travellers.
Riverwalk gives shelter for the night.
A player can buy and sell at Riverwalk.
Riverwalk opens a way on to somewhere else.
Talk at Riverwalk points to something elsewhere.
Riverwalk is a halt in a sheltered sea cove at the mouth of the pilgrim water, the channel up to Hissmir.
Boats off the Padomaic run put in at Riverwalk.
The houses stand on the shore.
A plank walk runs out from the houses across the cove to the islet where the ferry stage moors.
Canoes leave the ferry stage for Hissmir and Murkwater.
Riverwalk lives on the ferry stage and the toll on boats entering the pilgrim water.
Riverwalk feeds and lodges the boat crews.
Thorn's field-owners and the stewards of Hissmir both say the toll on the pilgrim water is theirs.
The plank walk is the only way between the shore and the ferry stage.
Everyone who lands at the ferry stage walks past the toll-holder's post at the shore end of the walk.
A totem stands on the shore.
The long house stands on piles in the shallows beside the shore houses.
The plank walk ends at a tent on a low islet.
The ferry stage is moored off the far side of the islet.
The crews' house is a plank house on posts, on dry ground at the shore.
The family house is a plank house on posts, on dry ground at the shore.
The plank walk is constantly re-planked and its boards are all different ages.
The boards record the order in which the village was built.
Boats pole across the cove to the ferry stage off the islet.
The toll is argued over nightly.
Paying the toll to either Thorn or Hissmir counts as taking its side.
The village is linear and sociable.
The palette is silver weathered plank, black water and reed thatch.
Boards run underfoot from the shore to the islet.
Poles push into the mud.
Talk carries over still water.
Boats would bypass Riverwalk if the cove silted up.
The villagers sound the way across the cove to the ferry stage every morning.
